unit.why: A moral exemplum on escorting the dead. A bedridden pious man is miraculously able to rise only for the righteous dead. Its moral, which leads into a homily on hypocrites, is that an apparent saint was a secret idolater and an apparent villain was saved by honouring his father. No Hasidic figures appear.

stories.start_quote: מעשה באיש אחד שהי׳ צדיק בכל דרכיו
stories.summary_en: A pious man who always escorted the dead becomes lame and prays to be able to rise when a righteous corpse passes. When he fails to rise for a revered elder but rises for a known villain, two elders investigate. They find that the villain had devotedly honoured his aged father, while the revered man secretly kept a golden idol with a cross in a locked room.

tags.why: Exemplary tale framed as a lesson on the mitzvot of escorting the dead and honouring parents
